title: A number that springs back says why it did
goal: Type a width a layer will not take and the box comes back to the width it kept, with nothing to say why. Anyone watching sees a box that ignored them rather than a layer that refused. The line under Position & Size should carry the reason for a few seconds, the way it already does when you click a number you cannot type.
notes:
Decided in docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md section 4, "What a control shows after a set the picked things refused": nothing moved at all -> the control returns to the value it had AND the line under the section carries the reason, in the wording law two halves, with no toast. The read-back half landed on 2026-09-06 (GeometryNumberField now sets then re-reads geometrySelection); this is the half that was left.

GeometryInspector.swift already has the mechanism: `explaining: LayerGeometryField?` puts a sentence in the caption line for 6 seconds, but it only answers for READ-ONLY fields via LayerGeometrySelection.explanation(for:). A refusal on a typeable field needs its own state and its own sentence. The reason itself is not in LayerGeometrySelection today: LayerGeometryEditing.minimumWidth only knows the text floor, while a group refused by its own flow (GroupLayout.minWidth/maxWidth, the Layout section Smallest and Largest rows) is refused inside Layer.resized(to:). Either plumb the group layout limits into LayerGeometryEditing so note(for:) warns before you type as well, or work the sentence out from the before/after pair the commit already has.

Scripts/playtest/width-reads-back-walk.json is the walk that sets a Smallest width of 160 on a Button and types 50.

Triage 2026-09-07, design review: the line under a section is now doing three jobs with no shared rule, so settle the rule here rather than adding a fourth use of it later. The three: the standing caption ('Up or down arrow steps by 1, Shift by 10'), the six second explanation of why a number cannot be typed, and the refusal reason this task adds. Evidence: audit 2026-09-06-a-decided-number-looks-decided rough 4 says the standing caption still promises stepping on three fields that are now plain text, and the same audit records a stale-explanation bug where the six second message outlived the rule it was explaining.
acceptance: Typing a width the picked layers refuse puts a plain sentence in the line under Position & Size
The sentence names the rule that refused it, not the field
The line goes back to its usual caption on its own, and at once if a different layer is picked
Nothing at all is said when the layers take the number as typed
One rule is written down for that line and every use of it follows: what it may say, which message wins when two want it at once, and how long each stays
The standing caption under Position & Size stops describing controls that are not there, so a section whose numbers are mostly plain text does not still promise arrow key stepping
Verified in the probe with a real screen capture

log.note: Triage 2026-09-07: folded in the design review finding that the line under a panel section is doing three jobs with no shared rule. Two acceptance items added.

Adversarial review before building. (1) Walked it cold: set Smallest width 160 on a stack, type 50, the box snaps to 160 and the line under the fields answers, in the same place and with the same quiet-to-ordinary strength shift a click on a plain number already uses. No new vocabulary, no toast. (2) The mock assumes the panel knows WHY, and it does not: a group's Smallest and Largest are applied by its own flow inside resized(to:), and LayerGeometryEditing had never heard of them. Rather than guessing a sentence from the before/after pair, plumb those limits in. That also makes the hover note ("Will not go below 160 px") true BEFORE you type, which is the cheaper half of the same value. (3) Cut: no highlighting of the Layout section's Smallest row. That is a second mechanism for one job and the line already answers. (4) Shortest version: do not add a fourth state to the line. Collapse the two answer states it already has into ONE answer with one lifetime and one precedence rule, which is less code than today plus a case. (5) The sentence must never be HELD as a string, or it outlives its rule for six seconds (the exact bug audit 2026-09-06-a-decided-number-looks-decided recorded). Hold what you did, work the words out afresh each draw. (6) Measured what actually refuses: a hug stack with no limits TAKES a width of 50 and lets its contents overflow, and the text width floor (80) and text height floor are already declared. So the group's Smallest/Largest were the only undeclared refuser; the un-nameable fallback is a last resort, not the common path. (7) X and Y are never refused (nothing clamps a position), so the sentence is a size question only.

Built and verified in the probe (Screen Recording granted, so real window captures). What landed: (a) LayerSizeRule/LayerSizeHold in PhotonzCore carry a limit that knows its own name, and LayerGeometryEditing now reads a group's own Smallest and Largest (GroupLayout min/max width and height) so the panel knows the limits its flow was going to apply anyway. (b) LayerGeometrySelection.refusal(asking:for:landedOn:) is the sentence, worked out live from what you DID rather than held as words. (c) GeometryInspector's two answer states collapsed into one Answer enum with one lifetime, one precedence rule (newest wins) and one six second fade. (d) caption stops describing controls that are not there: it names the letters an arrow really steps, and where nothing types it points at clicking instead. (e) The rule for the line is written into UX-PATTERNS section 4 as 'The line under a section', and the doc bumped to v1.5. Side effects worth knowing: the W hover tip now warns before you type, and a typed size is clamped to the group's limits on the way out instead of being handed to the flow to bounce back. Post-build review, honestly: the sentence points at a row visible in the same panel a few lines below, which is the best part; the down arrow at the floor now explains itself too, which was not asked for and is welcome; 'holds this at 160 px' reads oddly with several layers picked; a one-line caption becoming a two-line answer nudges the section below down for six seconds, which is how the existing click answer has always behaved. Tests: 4952 green. Walk: Scripts/playtest/refused-width-says-why-walk.json, 50 steps, ok. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-08-refused-size-says-why.json with three real captures.
